title: Strategy as a set of choices
purpose: Frame a strategy workshop without invented performance claims

slides.headline:
Choose where
not to compete.
slides.message: A workshop framework for turning broad ambition into explicit choices.
slides.source: Author-authored decision framework; recommendations, not empirical business findings.

slides.headline: Separate aspiration from a decision.
slides.message: An aspiration describes intent; a decision commits resources and accepts a trade-off.
slides.source: Author-authored decision framework; recommendations, not empirical business findings.

columns.title: Aspiration
columns.body: “Be the most useful partner.” Useful as a direction, insufficient as a resource choice.

columns.title: Decision
columns.body: Prioritize one customer problem, name the owner and define what will be deferred.

slides.headline: Make the assumptions visible.
slides.message: A choice links a problem to a testable expectation.
slides.source: Author-authored decision framework; recommendations, not empirical business findings.

slides.headline:
A roadmap is not
the strategy.
slides.message: A delivery sequence is useful only when it serves a clearly stated choice.
slides.source: Author-authored decision framework; recommendations, not empirical business findings.

slides.headline:
Leave with a choice,
not another slogan.
slides.message: Record the commitment, the trade-off, the accountable owner and the date for review.
slides.source: Author-authored decision framework; recommendations, not empirical business findings.
